title: fix(metadata-protocol): an object's references list a permission set named only by its `fields` keys (#23539)
body:
Fixes #23539

Clause-②: no

## Summary

`findReferencesToMeta` serves `GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/references`, the admin "Used by" panel. It now lists a permission set that names an object only in its `fields` keys. `PermissionSetSchema.fields` is keyed `OBJECT.FIELD`, and the security plugin applies a set's field rules to an object by that key prefix (`PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions`). Before this change, such a set was missing from the object's answer. The panel could then read "Safe to delete." while the set still masked the object's fields.

## What changed

- **`packages/metadata-protocol/src/reference-sites.ts`.** A composite-key seed, `COMPOSITE_KEY_REFERENCE_SITES`: `permission.fields` names an `object` through the text before a key's first `.`. It is exposed as a new index member, `compositeKeyByTarget`, and kept OUT of `byTarget`.
  - Both premises are derived from the schemas, in the `nameVocabularyRejectsKey` style, and fail closed. `permission` must still declare `fields` as a root record, and `ObjectSchema.name` must still reject `.`. If either stops holding, the seed drops out and the derivation pin goes red.
  - The seed's target is typed `'object'` alone.
  - `nameVocabularyRejectsKey`'s schema read is factored into `nameVocabularyVerdict`. Its answers are unchanged: the existing `unanswerableTargetTypes` pins still pass.
- **`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, two regions only.**
  - A new `collectCompositeKeyHeadHits`, placed beside `collectReferenceHits`. `referencedNamesAt` and `collectReferenceHits` are byte-unchanged.
    - It reads only the seeded root record's keys, and matches the text before the FIRST `.` (dot index above 0).
    - A key's field part is never read. A key with no object part (`.full_name`) names no object.
    - One row per site, at path `fields{key}`.
  - `findReferencesToMeta` folds the composite sites into the same one-read-per-source-type matchers. The new row's kind is `permission fields`. Every existing row, the response shape and the `field` target's 501 are unchanged.
- **`duplicatePackage` is not touched,** and its `byTarget.get('object')` reading is unchanged.

### Why the seed is not a `byTarget` row

This was measured in round 1 (report comment 6179812710, experiment E1) with a plain `{ permission, fields, object }` row in `byTarget`. The answer did not change, because the walk compares a WHOLE value with the object's name. And `duplicatePackage` broke. It reads `byTarget.get('object')` as a flat set of object-naming property names, so a copied object's own `fields` key was renamed. `protocol-duplicate-package-unprefixed-object.test.ts` went red, with `noteCopy.fields.ticket` undefined. The derivation pin now asserts that `byTarget('object')` has no `permission.fields` site.

### Why the split is the first `.`

`ObjectSchema.name` and `FieldSchema.name` are both `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`, so neither can contain `.`. The evaluator (`key.startsWith(object + '.')`), lint `security-fls-unknown-field` and `duplicatePackage`'s field-rule rewrite all make the same split.

Save-door readings (`saveMetaItem`, real kernel):
- A deeper key on an in-stack object (`customer.full_name.extra`) is refused with 422 `security-fls-unknown-field`.
- A bare key is refused with 422 `security-fls-unqualified-key`.
- A key for an out-of-stack object (`no_such_object.x`) and an empty-object-part key (`.full_name`) are stored.

## Evidence (final head `8ca891b1d5`)

- **Real-kernel pin**, `packages/objectql/src/protocol-references-permission-field-keys.test.ts`: ObjectKernel + ObjectQLPlugin + memory driver; every item passes the real save door.
  - On `main` (round 1, `9e67e008e1` over `7b64a3d73d`): `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`. The two failures were `expected [ Array(1) ] to include 'refsrc_customer_fls@fields{key}'` and `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'refsrc_invoice_fls@fields{key}' ]`.
  - After the fix: `Tests 4 passed (4)`.
  - The pin covers four cases. (1) The set is listed at `fields{key}`. (2) Negative control: a set whose keys name only another object is not listed, even where its FIELD part spells the asked object; it is listed once for the object it does name. (3) The `objects{key}` row is unchanged. (4) The `field` target still refuses with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / 501.
- **`field` target byte-identity.** A real-kernel probe captured `findReferencesToMeta({ type: 'field', name: 'refsrc_customer.full_name' })` before and after the fix. Both runs gave `NOT_IMPLEMENTED 501 refusal:true`, message sha256 `7b4aee8698a564f69599ba38e1b3f54ec2623cd5336a8e57e267b093ea4b2457`. The probe was a throwaway file, deleted afterwards.
  - Before, `refsrc_customer` answered the grant row only. After, it answers that same row plus the new `fields{key}` row.
- **Ablation.** The walk branch was deleted: the line calling `collectCompositeKeyHeadHits` in `findReferencesToMeta`.
  - Mutation: `ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1→0, blob `5be7b1c1adc7`→`09028903ed91`.
  - Positive control on the pristine build: the call marker is present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`.
  - The rebuild's ESM/CJS emitted. DTS refused with TS6133 (the helper was now unused), which does not affect the JS artifacts the suite loads.
  - `ablation-dist-preflight --absent`: marker absent from dist.
  - Pin: `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`, the same two listing assertions.
  - Restore: blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty. The rebuild re-emitted both declaration files (`check-dts-emitted 2/2`). Preflight: marker present in both JS files, and the tree is clean. Pin: `Tests 4 passed (4)`.
- **Suites.**
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run`: `Test Files 236 passed | 3 skipped (239)`, `Tests 28412 passed | 19 skipped`.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local`: `Test Files 419 passed (419)`, `Tests 8112 passed`. This includes `protocol-references`, `protocol-duplicate-package-unprefixed-object` and `protocol-duplicate-package-permission-field-keys`.
  - `reference-sites.derivation.test.ts`: `Tests 25 passed (25)`.
- **Typecheck.**
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0. `--listFiles` includes `reference-sites.ts`, `protocol.ts` and `reference-sites.derivation.test.ts`.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: exit 0, with `check:test-typecheck: OK — 40 file(s) / 234 error(s) / 65 pinned signature(s) held`.
- **Derived gates** at `8ca891b1d5`: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands from the 5 changed paths. All 67 were run, each exit captured before any pipe. 66 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET: it needs about 70 packages built, which this worktree does not hold, so it is NOT MEASURED here and CI builds them. `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` first exited 3 on a missing `packages/objectql/dist`; after an objectql build it was re-measured at exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: `67 derived, 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. The 11 wide-population families and the 6 workflow-valued families are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- The new row's path spelling `fields{key}` follows the existing `objects{key}` grammar. A set naming an object in both `objects` and `fields` answers two rows, one per path. That is the walk's existing one-row-per-path behaviour.
- Noted, not filed: the `field` target's refusal text says every property that names a field holds the bare field name. `permission.fields` is the one derived field site whose keys are the composite form, so the sentence is inaccurate for that one site. The refusal itself stays honest, and the card keeps the `field` answer unmoved.
- Noted, not filed: `duplicatePackage` reads `byTarget('object')` as a source-type-blind property-name set. This is why the seed lives in its own map, and the derivation pin guards it.
- A save-door finding about the empty-object-part FLS key (`.full_name`) went to the seat for filing. It is out of this PR's scope.
